draft.title: Gender and identity
card: the social roles and expectations that a society attaches to being a man, a woman or another identity. These can differ between cultures and can change over time.
a person's sense of who they are. It can include gender, family, culture, beliefs and interests.
Gender is shaped by society, so expectations about it are learned. A person's own sense of identity can match those expectations or differ from them.
A person's gender can be one part of their identity. Identity is wider than gender, and each person's identity is their own.
draft.remember: Gender is what society expects. Identity is how a person sees themselves.

a.q: Which example best shows a gender expectation?
opts: A community expects boys to take on certain jobs
A teenager enjoys painting and chess
A student feels proud of her family's heritage
A man describes himself as a quiet person
a.why: A community expecting people to act or work a certain way because of their gender is a social role or expectation. The other options describe a person's own interests or sense of self, which relate to identity, not to what society expects of a gender.
a.clue: Which one is about what society expects of a group?

b.q: Sam grew up in a town where people expected men to work in trades. Sam trains as a nurse and says, "I know who I am and what I want to do." Which statement fits this case?
opts: Sam's sense of identity differs from the town's expectation
Sam's gender expectation is the same as Sam's identity
The town's expectations form Sam's identity and must match
Sam has no identity because he ignores gender expectations
b.why: The town's expectation is a gender expectation, while Sam's sense of who he is makes up his identity. The card says identity can differ from expectations. The tempting option that the two are the same is wrong, because expectations come from society and identity comes from the person.
b.clue: Separate what the town expects from how Sam sees himself.

a.best: A community expects boys to take on certain jobs

b.best: Sam's sense of identity differs from the town's expectation
